questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to experience the Italian culture and be more familiar with the language.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found it easy to find the information needed upon arrival. It is easier to find the information when you are there in person, than online.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had to register at the school when we arrived, and afterwards we got a email telling where to go for the first day of school.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I lived with three danish girls. We found an apartment through a website called 'housinganywhere'. We signed the contract in february, six months before our exchange in august, so it was pretty cheap compared to other Milan prices. We paid 4400 kroner each person.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Be aware of the public transportation possibilities from your home to campus, since biking is not really optimal in Milan.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to meet at the office with Massimo. The office was under construction, so it was a bit difficult to find it, but otherwise it was easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I did not get any additional help than registrering

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes i wished for

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You don't have to be too stressed about the registration process. They are very easy going in Italy and often you find a way if something comes up!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I would recommend to do the MA classes, since the level of these are most similar to the BA level in Denmark. I took one course on the BA level which was very different from what i study at home, so the BA level was suitable

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: They almost only did lectures. There were not really any class discussions or smaller classes to elaborate on the lectures.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Political order, violence and institutions
Global criminal organizations
Globalization, social justice and human rights
Microeconomics of uncertainty

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend the course 'Political order, violence and institutions' since the teacher was very good and almost all the topics were interesting and relevant when studying social sciences.

If taking the 'Global criminal organizations' course i would recommend to be non-attending student, since the teacher was not the best, and you had to show up for class for at least 80% of the time. The topic though was interesting, since it was about the italian mafia and women's role in the mafia.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There were no unexpected costs

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The public transportation was only 22 euro per month if you sign up for a travel card. The only thing you need to register for this is a tax code. I would recommend to book a time for getting the tax code before you get to Milan, since there can be some waiting time.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I did not attend any offers from the school

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There are so many museums, cafes, restaurants and markets. The navigli market every tuesday and saturday is very good.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
It is very easy to go to como lake (only 40 minutes by train). It is very beautiful to both hike and go for a boat ride.
There are so many possibilities to visit other italian cities. the flixbus is very cheap. Fx Naples, Rome, Bologna...

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, everything is more chill in italy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find the differences challenging, but i just had to adjust to things taking more time than in Denmark

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Cheap coffee and the sun

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Enjoy the Italian culture
Consider where in Milan you are staying, since most of the time is outside the school

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: When you begin at the school the first week is ment for you to try the different courses. Also you can always change courses during the semester.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living in Navigli was a great experience, since this was a very local area, where it was possible to experience the everyday italian culture

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Living in a foreign country can sometimes be overwhelming since everything is new in the beginning

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
